subject: Adoption signals & commit recommendation for renewal
messages:
From: Maya Ramesh <maya@harbor.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@harbor.ai
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 usage / renewal checkpoint — can we align?

Diego,

Hope you’re well — our team is pulling together a concise health review ahead of our August renewal and wanted to align on a few data points and suggestions before we lock terms. Quick context: since adopting Redwood in Jan we’ve seen 3x MVT traffic for two core features (article-summarizer and response-suggest) and token mix is shifting toward embedding-heavy calls for similarity searches.

Can you share: 1) a short breakdown of token spend by model family for last 90 days, 2) any latency regressions or performance notes you’ve seen from the service side, and 3) a recommended commit tier that balances current run-rate + expected Q4 growth (~25–30% q/q). Procurement included here for rough timing.

We can do a 30-min sync next week — are you available Tues 6/26 10–11am PT?

Thanks,
Maya Ramesh
Head of Ops, Harbor Analytics
M: +1 (415) 555-0142

[Attachment: harbor-q2-usage-export.csv (CSV export of token-level usage by endpoint, 90d)]

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Maya Ramesh <maya@harbor.ai>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, procurement@harbor.ai
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 16:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Q2 usage / renewal checkpoint — can we align?

Maya — thanks for the note and for the CSV. Quick read-through shows the embedding-heavy shift you mentioned and a clear weekday peak between 14:00–18:00 PT that correlates with your QA pipeline. I pulled together a short ops/ROI packet and a recommended commit ladder with three scenarios (status-quo, conservative growth, and accelerated adoption). See attached PDF + ROI workbook.

High-level observations (TL;DR):
- Token mix: ~62% embedding tokens (similarity queries) vs 28% generation, 10% other (reranking / analytics).
- Cost drivers: peak-hour concurrency and repeated cold KV loads for the summarizer. We recommend enabling prefix caching for summarizer flows + a small dedicated capacity pool for embedding-heavy endpoints to flatten cost.
- Suggested commit: mid-tier (Reserved-100k tokens/day equivalent) reduces unit cost by ~22% vs pay-as-you-go; accelerated tier (Reserved-150k) gives 34% savings and covers expected Q4 spike.

Ask: can procurement share a target monthly commitment range? I’ve tentatively blocked Tue 6/26 10am PT — if that works I’ll send calendar invite and a 1-pager for procurement.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

[Attachments: harbor-ops-report-q2.pdf, ROI-calculation-harbor.xlsx]

---- Original CSV analysis included inline below for convenience ----

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Ramesh <maya@harbor.ai>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, procurement@harbor.ai
Date: Sat, 23 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 usage / renewal checkpoint — can we align?

Maya — looping in an abbreviated commercial proposal and the limited-time uplift credits for new commits. Diego covered the ops side; a few commercial notes to make the discussion concrete before we meet:

- Proposal snapshot (for discussion on Tue):
  • Option A — Baseline: 90k tokens/day reserved (12-month) — ~22% unit saving, standard SLA
  • Option B — Growth: 120k tokens/day reserved (12-month) — ~30% unit saving + 10% uplift credit applied in months 1–3
  • Option C — Acceleration: 150k tokens/day reserved (annual) — ~34% unit saving + 25% free burst credits for two quarters and two dedicated GPU slots for peak windows

- Commercial caveat: credits and burst slots require procurement approval and simple amendment to our standard T&Cs; we can draft a short addendum and route via your procurement team.
- Ops enablement: Marissa will lead the technical onboarding for the dedicated pool and hit the two-day runbook for prefix caching; Monica will be primary CS contact for QoS monitoring.

If you can share a target monthly spend window or the internal approval cadence, I’ll include that in the invite notes. Otherwise, Tuesday 6/26 10am PT confirmed from our side. Calendar invite incoming.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Manager, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: commercial-snapshot-HARB-2028-04.pdf (proposal summary)]

From: Maya Ramesh <maya@harbor.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@harbor.ai, ops@harbor.ai
Date: Sat, 23 Jun 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 usage / renewal checkpoint — can we align?

Diego, Jordan — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear options. Procurement prefers Option B as the primary path but would like a two-month ramp clause (start-of-term credits applied while we onboard the dedicated pool). Key asks ahead of Tue:

1) A short amendment draft that includes: ramp credits (months 1–2), SLA targets for the dedicated pool, and clear rollback if latency > 150ms p50 for two consecutive weeks.
2) A one-page runbook that Marissa can follow to enable prefix caching and validate warm KV behavior.
3) A final rough PO amount to run up to procurement for prelim approval — we’re targeting <$150k ARR threshold for fast-track approval.

If you can push the amendment + one-pager by Mon EOD (6/25) procurement will start intake. Looking forward to the call Tues 10am PT.

Best,
Maya Ramesh
Head of Ops, Harbor Analytics
